keys.title: Policy version
keys.help: Required. Always 1 for this version of the policy. An unknown version refuses to open apps.

keys.title: Organisation name
keys.help: Your organisation's name. Every message Krate shows about the policy uses it, for example "Acme Labs does not allow this app". Optional.

keys.title: Organisation on Krate
keys.help: The organisation on Krate's hub that these computers belong to: its short name, as in krate.tech/org/acme-labs. Krate shows that organisation's apps to the people signed in to it. Optional.

keys.title: Trusted signing roots
keys.help: The signing roots this computer trusts: each a name and the public half of an Ed25519 root key, as 64 hex characters. An app passes when its signature verifies and its root (the delegation's root, or the signing key itself) is listed. Empty or absent: no limit on roots.

keys.title: Allow unsigned apps
keys.help: Whether an app with no signature may open. Default: allowed when there is no [trust] section, refused when roots are listed. A signature that is present but damaged never passes, whatever this says.

keys.title: Allow apps signed by other roots
keys.help: Whether an app signed by a root that is not listed may open. Default: allowed when no roots are listed, refused when they are.

keys.title: Blocked capabilities
keys.help: Capabilities no app may be given on this computer, spelled as an app's manifest spells them (camera.capture, audio.capture, location.read, ui.clipboard, fs.write ...). Matched on the name before ':', so fs.write blocks every fs.write grant. A blocked capability is shown as blocked by your organisation and cannot be granted.

keys.title: Network ceiling
keys.help: The only hosts any app may connect to, whatever its manifest asks for. Same patterns as a manifest: host or *.host, then :port or :*. Absent: no ceiling.

keys.title: Proxy
keys.help: The proxy every connection Krate makes goes through, for http and https alike, as http://host:port (user:password@ allowed), or "direct" to use none. When set, it replaces the proxy variables (HTTPS_PROXY, HTTP_PROXY, ALL_PROXY, NO_PROXY) and the system's own proxy settings, so a person's shell cannot route around it; absent, the variables apply when set and the system's static proxy otherwise. This computer's own services (localhost) are always reached directly. Krate does not run a PAC script or WPAD; if your computers rely on one, set the proxy here.

keys.title: Hosts reached without the proxy
keys.help: Used with proxy: hosts reached directly, separated by commas, as NO_PROXY is written: an entry covers the host and every name under it (acme.com covers git.acme.com), * covers every host. Address ranges such as 10.0.0.0/8 are not read; name the hosts.

keys.title: Send usage counts
keys.help: Whether Krate sends its anonymous usage counts (install, make, open, publish) to Krate's hub. false: none are sent and the first-run question about them is not asked.

keys.title: Hub
keys.help: The only Krate hub this computer talks to for private apps, publishing and sign-in. Any other hub, from a flag or an environment variable, is refused.

keys.title: Allow AI builds
keys.help: false: Krate Studio and krate create refuse to start an AI build, before any AI provider is contacted.

keys.title: Allowed AI providers
keys.help: When present, only these AI providers may be used for a build. Provider ids: claude, codex, gemini, copilot, grok.

keys.title: Updates
keys.help: auto (the default): updates are offered as usual. notify: Krate checks for a new version and says so, and never installs one. off: Krate never checks.

keys.title: Open record location
keys.help: Where Krate appends its record of every app opened or refused on this computer, one JSON line each. Default: /var/log/krate/opens.jsonl on macOS and Linux, %ProgramData%\Krate\logs\opens.jsonl on Windows.

keys.title: Run apps on the interpreter
keys.help: true: every app runs on Krate's interpreter (Pulley) instead of compiled machine code, so Krate never makes executable memory. For endpoint protection that blocks code generated at run time, and Windows Arbitrary Code Guard. Apps may run slower this way.

app_rules.title: Organisation apps: no reading the clipboard
app_rules.help: false: the app cannot read the clipboard, and a paste the person makes into it is refused too.

app_rules.title: Organisation apps: no copying out
app_rules.help: false: nothing leaves the app by the clipboard.

app_rules.title: Organisation apps: no printing
app_rules.help: false: the app cannot print, or save as PDF from the print dialog.

app_rules.title: Organisation apps: kept out of screenshots
app_rules.help: false: the app's windows are kept out of screenshots, screen recordings and screen sharing where the system allows it (macOS and Windows; not Linux), and Krate takes no picture of the app itself.

app_rules.title: Organisation apps: delete team data when offline access ends
app_rules.help: true: when the app's offline access runs out, the app's team data on this computer is deleted at the next open.
